title: Spell Reviewer attention is treated as a finite budget, so a sensitive module onboarding evicts non-crucial items
content:
A.1.10.2.4.3.1.3 lets the Spell Crafter "request the removal of certain items if the Spell is deemed high risk, too big or contains novel code," noting that "such removals typically affect non-critical items, such as internal payments."

The sharper sentence follows: "Onboarding of sensitive modules is considered increasing the Spell's complexity in such a manner that the Spell Reviewers should only focus on this; therefore, non-crucial items should be removed from the Executive Sheet and included in the Executive Vote queue."

That is an explicit model of review as a scarce resource with a fixed budget per cycle. Reviewers are not assumed to scale with content; adding a twelfth item does not get a twelfth item's worth of scrutiny, it dilutes the eleven. Where one item genuinely requires the whole budget, the correct response is to empty the Spell around it.

The governance consequence is that a Spell's contents are not determined by what has been approved — everything here has already cleared its governance path — but by what can be *reviewed together safely*. Approval earns an item a place in the queue; review capacity determines which cycle it lands in.

The judgment call sits with the Crafter and Reviewers, i.e. with the people who will actually perform the scrutiny, rather than with the Governance Point assembling the sheet. Whoever bears the cognitive load holds the veto over the workload.
description: A.1.10.2.4.3.1.3 makes complexity the allocation currency: when reviewers should focus only on one item, everything else must move to the Executive Vote queue rather than compete for scrutiny.
